mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in PARKS together with stable-to-higher GROCERY_PHARM indicates broader out-of-home activity and errand bundling, which should lift RETAIL_REC within four weeks as discretionary trips spill over into shopping visits.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above its last-4-week mean within 28 days while PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both remain above their recent averages.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT turns less negative than the prior week, access friction to shopping districts falls and retail visits improve over the next one to two weeks; the signal should be visible quickly if commuting flows are normalizing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points week-on-week after being below -10
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase within 14 days after a week-on-week TRANSIT improvement of at least 3 points from a sub -10 level.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while WORKPLACES stay depressed, more time is spent at home and fewer shopping trips are made, so RETAIL_REC should drift lower over the next four weeks relative to the prior month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week average while RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline and WORKPLACES stay below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp negative shock in TRANSIT relative to WORKPLACES signals commuting disruption or access restrictions, which should suppress retail footfall within one week by reducing trips to shopping corridors and mixed-use centers.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls at least 5 points below WORKPLACES week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower in the following week after TRANSIT deteriorates by at least 5 points more than WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: In a holiday-shopping regime, a rebound in PARKS combined with weaker WORKPLACES indicates leisure-oriented time allocation and shorter commuting days, which should increase RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as people shift toward shopping and outings.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its prior 4-week mean despite PARKS rising and WORKPLACES remaining below baseline for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM stays above baseline while RETAIL_REC remains weak, the grocery run is not substituting into discretionary retail; instead it signals routine errand traffic that should keep RETAIL_REC flat to slightly lower over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises materially within 14 days even though GROCERY_PHARM stays above baseline and no corresponding rise appears in TRANSIT or WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT below their recent means indicates fewer cross-town trips and weaker weekday mobility, which should reduce RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as routine shopping is deferred.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain below their previous 2-week averages
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not underperform its last-month mean after both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay below their recent averages for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT from a depressed level after restrictions ease should reach retail districts quickly, producing a one-week improvement in RETAIL_REC; the mechanism fails if transit recovers but retail does not, implying the mobility gain is not translating into shopping visits.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -15 after at least one week below -15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the week after TRANSIT crosses above -15 from below -15.
